You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:

# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Has the woman's jacket moved toward being closed in the edited image compared with the source image, without being fully closed?
node.criteria: Pass only if the edited jacket shows a visible change toward closure compared with the source jacket, but still has a visible opening. Fail if there is no visible movement toward closure or the jacket is unchanged or more open. Unknown only if the jacket's state or change is not sufficiently visible to assess.
node.binding: Compare the woman's jacket in the edited image with the source image to assess whether it has moved toward closure. This check records partial progress only; it does not satisfy the requirement for the jacket to be fully closed.

node_traces.evidence: The source jacket is visibly open at the front. In the edited image, it is still open and appears to flare farther away from her body; there is no visible movement toward closure.

response.content: {"text":"The trace is a valid, high-confidence visual observation—not a transport, schema, or dependency failure—and it specifically reports that the edited jacket flares farther open, which is evidence against partial progress. The reference “yes” is an aggregate constraint, not proof that this check’s atomic criterion is met; do not flip the decision or weaken the visible-change requirement just to match it. Inspect whether the node’s binding and criterion correctly distinguish jacket closure from pose, viewpoint, and garment motion, and whether the comparison is anchored to the same jacket/front opening in both images. The edited pose differs substantially, so avoid treating apparent flare alone as decisive if alignment or visibility makes the change uncertain; use unresolved only when the visual evidence genuinely cannot establish the change. Preserve the distinction between partial movement toward closure and the instruction’s fully-closed completion criterion, and investigate any mismatch between this check and the aggregate/reference labeling."}
